from_text: The alignment of national legislation with the EU Regulation on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market (eIDAS Regulation) was further delayed.
to_text: As the national legislation is harmonised with the eIDAS Regulation of 2014, the country needs to take steps to align its laws with the revised 2024 version of the Regulation, establishing the new EU Digital Identity framework, which includes the setting up of a national Digital Identity Wallet .
basis: The 2023 report says eIDAS alignment was further delayed, while the 2024 report says national legislation is harmonised with the 2014 eIDAS Regulation, and the list of amendments to the law in MKD-GOV-2025-009-0003 shows none between the two reports.

from_text: (*) This law aligns with Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as regards establishing the European Digital Identity Framework, CELEX no. 32024R1183.
to_text: Although the Law on Electronic Document, Electronic Identification and Trust Services does not fully align with the new EU Digital Identity Regulation, the Commission concludes that, for the purposes of the Reform Agenda step, North Macedonia has reached sufficient alignment with the EU acquis.
basis: The footnote to the consolidated law says it aligns with Regulation (EU) 2024/1183, while the Commission payment assessment of the same 2025 text says it does not fully align with that Regulation.

from_text: North Macedonia repo rts to have completed all preparatory activities for inclusion in the trusted list, including the assessment of two national trust service providers of electronic signatures.
to_text: To achieve this step, North Macedonia will need to finalise its self-assessment using the Commission’s standardised checklist, publish its national Trusted List in the required technical format with the necessary EU -specified extensions, and share with the Commission the information requested (namely, a signed version of the national trusted list and a signing certificate).
basis: North Macedonia reports having completed all preparatory activities for the trusted list, while the Commission says it still needs to finalise its self-assessment and publish its national trusted list in the required format.

from_text: The beneficiary considers this step as achieved.
to_text: On this basis, the Commission considers the step as not achieved.
basis: On the same trusted list step in the same assessment, the beneficiary considers it achieved and the Commission considers it not achieved.

from_text: The national interoperability fr amework has been aligned with the European interoperability framework 2.0.
to_text: North Macedonia should ensure alignment with both the European Interoperability Framework (latest revision in 2017) and the Interoperable Europe Act (2022).
basis: The 2023 screening report says the national framework has been aligned with European Interoperability Framework 2.0, while the 2023 report says the country should ensure alignment with that framework, naming its latest revision of 2017.

from_text: The once-only principle is applied.
to_text: Practice shows that the main reason why there is almost no communication between public bodies electronically is insufficient technical equipment and readiness of institutions for this kind of communication.
basis: North Macedonia tells the 2023 screening that the once-only principle is applied, while its 2023 reform strategy says there is almost no electronic communication between public bodies.

from_text: The once-only principle is applied.
to_text: Namely, despite Law on General Administrative Procedures has been in force for 9 years already, institutions still do not gather evidence ex officio, as prescribed with the law.
basis: North Macedonia tells the 2023 screening that the once-only principle is applied, while its 2024 Reform Agenda says institutions still do not gather evidence ex officio as the law prescribes.

from_text: The use of the interoperability system slightly increased during the reporting period, although many institutions do not use it despite having installed equipment and software.
to_text: Analysis of platform traffic over the last 4 years shows an annual decline in traffic in the period 2019-2021.
basis: The 2020 report says use of the interoperability system slightly increased in its reporting period, while the State Audit Office finds an annual decline in platform traffic over 2019 to 2021.

from_text: Regarding the EU Business Registers Interconnection System (BRIS), North Macedonia stated that it is ready technically to interconnect with BRIS to exchange information on companies, branches, on mergers, conversions and divisions, and on disqualification of directors.
to_text: It will, however, need to align with acquis provisions on structured/machine-readable data to be able to interconnect with the EU Business Registers Interconnection System (BRIS) in the future.
basis: North Macedonia states it is technically ready to interconnect with BRIS, while the Commission says it will need to align on structured or machine-readable data to be able to interconnect.
